newsitem.title: MEXICO: Wave of defections hits Mexico ruling party.
newsitem.headline: Wave of defections hits Mexico ruling party.

text.p: President Ernesto Zedillo's party suffered the latest in a string of defections on Wednesday when a congresswoman quit to join the main left-wing opposition.
Virginia Betanzos, a legislator from the southeastern state of Quintana Roo, announced her resignation from the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) in a speech to lower house deputies.
"There are no guarantees of free expression of ideas or of physical safety (in the PRI)", Betanzos said.
She claimed that PRI dissidents in her state had been beaten up by party thugs who enjoyed legal impunity.

PRI chiefs in Mexico City ignored repeated complaints about the matter so she had reluctantly decided to quit after 20 years and join the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), the main left-wing opposition, she said.

Betanzos was the third legislator to quit the PRI in the past three weeks in protest at the growing influence of party "dinosaurs" -- hardliners who want to turn back the clock on reforms and preserve the party's 67-year-old grip on power.
A former PRI state governor, Dante Delgado, also left the party recently to join a small left-wing splinter party and other PRI politicians are said to be considering quitting.

Alejandro Rojas Diaz-Duran, a Mexico City congressman who walked out last month to become an independent, told Reuters he believed the PRI had no future because it wanted to cling to power at all costs rather than make itself a modern democratic party.
"The dinosaurs are stronger than ever," he said. "I don't think the PRI has any future at all. It views dissent rather like AIDS -- something to be avoided like the plague."
Both Rojas and Layda Sansores, a PRI senator who quit last Tuesday to join the PRD, predicted that more ruling party politicians and militants would leave soon.
